sentences.text: 1 order dated 25.08.2023 passed by Ld. MM-04/Mahila Court/South District in Cr. Case no.4762/2022 pertaining to FIR No.547/2021, PS Ambedkar Nagar whereby charge for offence 498A/34 IPC was ordered to framed against revisionists Harish Sharma, Naresh Sharma and Om Kaur.
Charge for the offence u/s 379 IPC was ordered to be framed against all of them.

2. Briefly stated the facts as per record are as under:-
FIR No. 547 for the offences u/s 498A/406/34 IPC was lodged at PS Ambedkar Nagar on 21.09.2021 on the basis of written complaint of Ms. Sushma Kaushik dated 12.10.2020 forwarded by CAW Cell.
After completion of investigation, all the revisionists were charge-sheeted for the offences U/s 498A/406/34 IPC.
Cognizance was taken by Ld. Magistrate on 30.07.2022 and they were summoned as accused for next date of hearing i.e., 28.09.2022.
After hearing arguments from both the sides,
charge for the offences U/s 498A/34 IPC was ordered to be framed against revisionists Harish Sharma, Naresh Sharma and Om Kaur vide order dated 25.08.2023.
Charge was also directed to be framed against all the revisionists for the offence u/s 379 IPC.
That order is being challenged in these proceedings.
3. Arguments heard.
Cr Rev 410/2023 Harish Sharma & Ors. Vs. State Page 2/8 SUNIL GUPTA 4.

entities.text: Cr Rev 410/2023 Harish Sharma & Ors. Vs. State Page 2/8 SUNIL GUPTA
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It has been argued by Ld. Counsel for the revisionists that Ld. Trial Court has passed the impugned order in a mechanical manner without properly appreciating the material on record.
It has been submitted that the complainant had stayed at her matrimonial home hardly for a period of 11 days in total so, they was no question of any harassment having done to her during that time.
It has been further submitted that revisionist Narender @ Kala was differently abled and could not have committed the alleged offence.

It has been submitted that the complainant in her complaint on the basis of which present FIR was registered has mentioned about her entire jewelery having been snatched by the revisionists, however her brother in his statement u/s 161 Cr.P.C. has stated that he was told by the complainant regarding a jewelery articles having been kept by her mother-in-law.
It has been submitted that this contradiction was sufficient to create a doubt on the case of prosecution.
He has prayed for setting-aside the impugned order and for discharge of revisionists.
5. Same has been vehemently opposed by Ld. Addl. PP for State submitting that there was no illegality in the impugned order.
It has been submitted that material on record was sufficient to show a prima facie case against the revisionists and prosecution has been rightly given an opportunity to prove its case.
He has prayed for dismissal of revision petition.
6. I have considered the submissions from both the sides alongwith record.

7. Relevant portion of said order is reproduced below for ready reference:-
"6.

A perusal of the charge-sheet shows that the complainant has specifically named three accused persons i.e. the husband Harish Sharma, father in law Naresh Sharma and mother in law Om Kaur and stated that they used to demand dowry of Rs.25,00,000/- and also beat the complainant.
However, no such specific allegation has been made against accused Narender @ Kala.

The offence under Section 498A/34 IPC is hence made out against accused Harish Sharma, Naresh Sharma and Om Kaur, however, it is not made out against accused Narender who is discharged from the offence under Section 498A/34 IPC.
7.
The complainant has also made the allegation that all four accused persons were involved in forcibly snatching away her jewelery and keeping it with themselves.
An no entrustment has been mentioned, the offence punishable under Section 379 IPC is made out against the accused persons and not the offence under Section 406 IPC.

8. In view of the above discussion, this Court is of the view that prima facie commission of the offence under Section 498A/34 IPC is made out against the accused persons Harish Sharma, Naresh Sharma and Om Kaur.
Offence u/s 379 IPC is made out against all four accused persons and they are discharged for the offence under Section 406 IPC."

8. Perusal of record shows that the complainant has specifically made following allegations in her written complaint on the basis of which present FIR has been registered:-
"That on 5.5.2020 the husband of the applicant asked her to hand over entire jewellery to his mother.
When she protested she was beaten by her husband, her mother-in-law and her father-in-law and all the three Digitally signed by SUNIL SUNIL GUPTA Date:
16:09:43  +0530 respondents collectively and forcibly snatched her entire jewelery and took control thereof.
Her Dever Kala also assisted them in snatching the jewellery of the applicant."
9. Similarly, there are clear allegations in para 18 of her complaint regarding demand of dowry by revisionists Harish Sharma, Naresh Sharma and Om Kaur.
10. It is settled law that at the stage of framing of charge, the Court has to see as to whether a prima facie case is made out against the accused on the basis of material on record or not.

The Court is not Harish Sharma And Ors vs The State Nct Of Delhi on 7 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/49981098/
3 expected to minutely scrutinize the material on record at that stage to see if it is sufficient for conviction or not.

Reliance is placed on the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court titled as Onkar Nath Mishra and Ors. Vs. State ( NCT of Delhi) and Anr. (2008) 2 SCC 561 in which it was held as under:-
"11.

entities.text: Onkar Nath Mishra and Ors. Vs. State ( NCT of Delhi)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is trite that at the stage of framing of charge the Court is required to evaluate the material and documents on record with a view to finding out if the facts emerging therefrom, taken at their face value, disclosed the existence of all the ingredients constituting the alleged offence.
At that stage, the Court is not expected to go deep into the probative value of the material on record.
What needs to be considered is whether there is a ground for presuming that the offence has been committed and not a ground for convicting the accused has been made out.

At this stage, even strong suspicion founded on material which leads the Court to form a presumptive opinion as to existence of the factual ingredients constituting the offence alleged would justify the framing of charge against the accused in respect of the commission of that offence."

Digitally signed by SUNIL SUNIL GUPTA GUPTA Date:
2023.11.07 16:10:46 +0530 11.

Similar observations were made by Hon'ble Supreme Court in State of Maharashtra & Ors. Vs. Som Nath Thapa and Ors. 1996 Cri.LJ 2448 in following words:-
"If on the basis of materials on record, a court could come to the conclusion that commission of the offence is a probable consequence, a case for framing of charge exists.

entities.text: State of Maharashtra & Ors. Vs. Som Nath Thapa and Ors. 1996 Cri.LJ 2448
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: To put it differently, if the Court were to think that the accused might have committed the offence it can frame the charge, though for conviction the conclusion is required to be that the accused has committed the offence.

It is apparent that at the stage of framing of charge, probative value of the materials on record cannot be gone into; the materials brought on record by the prosecution has to be accepted as true at that stage."

12. The submission of Ld. Defence Counsel to the effect that complainant had resided at her matrimonial home for a period of 11 days only and no harassment at the hand of revisionists was possible during that short period, is not of any help to his case as there is no provision in law specifying any minimum time period for a married lady to stay at her matrimonial home before making a complaint against her in-laws for commission of offence u/s 498A IPC.
Such an offence can be committed even during stay of a few hours only.

Similarly, the ground that revisionist Narender was physically disabled and for that reason, could not have committed the alleged offence u/s 379 IPC is not sufficient to discharge him as whether he was physically capable enough to commit the alleged offence, can be determined during trial after evidence is led by both the parties.

Alleged contradiction between the allegations as leveled by the complainant and statement of her brother u/s 161 Cr.P.C. pales into insignificance as statement of her brother is at best 'hearsay evidence'.

sentences.text: Here again, it will be for the prosecution to establish its case beyond reasonable doubt and revisionists cannot be discharged on this ground.
13. It is settled law that while exercising the power of revisional jurisdiction, this Court can interefere only when the impugned order is perverse or untenable in law.

Reliance is placed upon judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in Sanjaysinh Ramrao Chavan vs. Dattatray Gulabrao Phalke and others, 2015 (3) SCC 123 wherein it has been observed as under :
"14.....

entities.text: Sanjaysinh Ramrao Chavan vs. Dattatray Gulabrao Phalke and others, 2015 (3) SCC 123
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Unless the order passed by the Magistrate is perverse or the view taken by the court is wholly unreasonable or there is non-consideration of any relevant material or there is palpable misreading of records, the Revisional Court is not justified in setting aside the order, merely because another view is possible.
The Revisional Court is not meant to act as an appellate court.
The whole purpose of the revisional jurisdiction is to preserve the power in the court to do justice in accordance with the principles of criminal jurisprudence.
The revisional power of the court under Sections 397 to 401 CrPC is not to be equated with that of an appeal.

Unless the finding of the court, whose decision is sought to be revised, is shown to be perverse or untenable in law or is grossly erroneous or glaringly unreasonable or where the decision is based on no material or where the material facts are wholly ignored or where the judicial discretion is exercised arbitrarily or capriciously, the courts may not interfere with decision in exercise of their revisional jurisdiction."

13. Considering the above discussion, this Court is of the view that there is no illegality in the impugned order so as to justify interference by Digitally signed by SUNIL SUNIL GUPTA GUPTA Date:
2023.11.07 16:11:18 +0530 this Court in revisional jurisdiction.
Accordingly, the revision petition stands dismissed.
